resources.string: Add an image using its three-dot menu.
Wait for the image operation to finish.
Touch and hold a card to select multiple images.
This image is already in your library. Download another copy?
This download has already been added. Resume it in Downloads.
Progress saved. Resuming depends on server support.
Download cancelled; no image added to your library.
This USB host is occupied. Eject its image first.
No USB host found. Open the setup wizard.
This USB host does not support CD-ROM mode.
The kernel cannot select this access mode on this host.
Eject the image before changing its mode.
Empty file without a filesystem, ready for writing image contents.
FAT16: older devices and small images. Maximum image size: 2 GiB.
FAT32: broad compatibility. Each file is limited to 4 GiB minus 1 byte.
exFAT: large files, modern Windows, macOS and Linux.
ext4: for Linux. Windows cannot read it with built-in tools.
NTFS: large files and Windows compatibility. Writing on macOS requires additional support.
Btrfs: for Linux. Windows and macOS require additional software.
A sparse image uses less initial space and grows as data is written. Hashes read its full logical size.
Local processing requires at least %1$s of free space.
Keep at least %1$s free for filesystem metadata.
Allow USBDroid root access in KernelSU or Magisk, then check again.
Free space for the image and temporary copy, or select another folder.
Check your connection and the address, then retry or resume the download.
Eject the occupied image or choose another USB host and supported mode.
Safely eject the image, then try again.
Select the folder again and allow the app access.
Check the settings and try again. See details for the cause.
Automatic conversion failed; the downloaded original was kept.
Hiding keeps the files and does not free space.
Permanently delete %1$d files (%2$s) and their library entries? This cannot be undone.
External original files will also be deleted from their current locations.
Deleted %1$d of %2$d files. Remaining files were kept.
Use IMG and ISO images as a USB drive or CD-ROM on your computer.
